descs.en: She nearly ran him over at a street race and jumped off her bike to fight him. He complimented her intake manifold.

titles.en: The Masterpiece I Could Never Draw

ideaNote: Planned: 50 chapters. The Track · The House · The Chop Shop · The Drawing · Side stories.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Raiden Lin plays the cheerful, slightly useless Lin son so well that the Syndicate and the police both ignore him. In fact he draws the family’s safe houses, and knows the weak point of every building in the city. One night he’s standing in the middle of a street-race track sketching the golden ratio of a warehouse, and a motorbike nearly kills him.

Jia, Jinx to everyone who values their teeth, gets off the bike to beat some sense into him. He looks up, smiles, and tells her that her intake manifold is beautifully symmetrical. Nobody has ever looked at her like that. She has no idea what to do about it.

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
I’ve wanted to write these two since Raiden walked into Every Flower in the Shop with three builders and a roll of drawings. He’s the funniest person in the family and the one who has hidden the most.

This is a warm book with grease and flour in it. He cooks; she fixes; they argue mid-kiss and keep going. Each of them has one deep wound, his borderland childhood and her father’s chop shop, and the book takes those seriously too.

This is mostly a light book. Planned content includes:

• Street racing and motorcycle crashes

• A childhood spent hidden in a borderland safe house, away from family

• A violent father who runs a chop shop for the Syndicate
